humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark targets graduate/expert-level global history knowledge itself, built from the Seshat Global History Databank (coded by historians and archaeologists), and asks whether models know the historical presence/absence of features in polities, including the evidenced vs inferred distinction.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only multiple-choice questions generated from Seshat records (variable, polity, time frame) with four answer options.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Four-choice questions asking whether a characteristic was Present, Absent, Inferred Present or Inferred Absent for a polity and time frame; the paper frames this as testing historical factual knowledge and the distinction between evidenced and inferred facts. Models also give chain-of-thought reasoning before answering, but only the letter is scored.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single domain (global history knowledge) and a single task format derived from Seshat.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o, Llama-3-70B, Llama-3.1-70B (FP8), Llama-3.1-8B (FP8), Gemini-1.5-flash.

quantitative_metrics.note: Balanced accuracy and adjusted balanced accuracy (2-choice and 4-choice) with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.

published_after_march_2023.note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks track; evaluations executed August 2024.

summary: The paper introduces HiST-LLM, a benchmark converting the Seshat Global History Databank (36,000 data points, 600+ polities, 2,700+ references) into multiple-choice questions on expert-level history. Seven LLMs are evaluated, and performance is analysed by time period, world region, and variable category.
key_findings: 4-choice balanced accuracy ranges from 33.6% (Llama-3.1-8B) to 46.0% (GPT-4-Turbo), above the 25% random baseline but short of expert knowledge. 2-choice balanced accuracy ranges 57.6-63.2 (GPT-4o best). Models perform better on earlier periods (e.g. GPT-4-Turbo 55.3% for 8k-6k BCE vs 38.7% for 1.5k-2k CE). Regionally performance is fairly even but best in the Americas and worst in Oceania and Sub-Saharan Africa.
evaluation_unit: multiple-choice question (Seshat data point: variable, polity, time frame)
gold_upstream: Seshat: Global History Databank (Turchin et al. 2015 [10-12]); data coded by graduate-level research assistants under supervision of established scholars, with 14,000 of 36,000 points reviewed by experts, each linked to scholarly references and justification text.
facets_explanation: Reference answers are the Seshat codes (absent/present/inferred absent/inferred present), produced by research assistants supervised by scholars with expert review for about 14,000 of 36,000 points. The question gives only variable, polity and time frame, so answering requires external historical knowledge. The paper notes that the benchmark records inferred and contested knowledge, but scoring is a single exact-match key per item and annotator disagreement is not treated as a topic of analysis.
results_explanation: Table 1 lists GPT-4-turbo at 46.0 [45.5, 46.5] 4-choice balanced accuracy (best), and GPT-4o at 63.2 [62.7, 63.6] 2-choice. The format gap is derived from the same models in 4-choice vs 2-choice: GPT-4-turbo 46.0 vs 60.0 is 14 points, Llama-3-70B 39.5 vs 62.6 is about 23 points, Llama-3.1-70B 40.8 vs 62.6 is about 22 points; the 2-choice and 4-choice tasks differ in number of options and also in label set, so the largest gap is approximated here and is not a strict like-for-like comparison. Metric is balanced accuracy (recorded as 'other' because the controlled list has only plain accuracy). No human baseline is reported; the paper only suggests one as future work. Regional asymmetry is stated: models perform worst in Oceania and Sub-Saharan Africa and best in the Americas.

humanities_role.quote: we introduce a unique data set of graduate and expert academic level global history knowledge, Seshat: Global History Databank

dataset_size.quote: the dataset used in the current article comprises 383 variables with 36,000 data points across more than 600 polities, and over 2,700 references

evaluation_set_size.quote: To test LLMs’ knowledge, we convert the dataset into multiple-choice questions that we then feed into LLMs via prompts.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: We used a multi-shot approach, providing four examples demonstrating solutions to other questions

gold_source.quote: This dataset covers every major world region from the Neolithic period to the Industrial Revolution and includes information reviewed and assembled by history experts and graduate research assistants.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: we asked whether a certain variable (e.g., writing) was present, absent, inferred present, or inferred absent in a particular polity and time frame

answer_multiplicity.quote: Models are evaluated by checking if their answers match exactly with the correct answers.

gold_upstream_source.quote: Under the supervision of established scholars (professors and PhD-level researchers), research assistants (RAs) populate the database with accessible information from scholarly publications.

reported_format_gap.quote: This table also includes the benchmark in a 2-choice format (absent/present), for which models balanced accuracy ranges from 57.6 to 63.2

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: we also measure balanced accuracy using only the “Present” and “Absent” categories. We refer to this as the 2-choice balanced accuracy

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: Models typically perform best in the Americas, with the exepction of Llama-3.1-8B (East and Southeast Asia), while they perform the worst in Oceania and Sub-Saharan Africa.
